clues.title: Coverage: small island off a bigger coast
text: Jersey is a self-governing** island territory** in the Channel Islands, located off France’s northwestern coast. It is a British Crown Dependency, so for country streaks purposes it is counted as part of the United Kingdom.
clues.summary: A self-governing island off the north-west coast of France and a British Crown Dependency. For country streaks it counts as the UK.

clues.title: Landscape: winding lanes, hedges, sunny, older camera
text: The island is shaped by a unique mix of British and Norman influences. The many **winding roads** and hedgerows are reminiscent of English country lanes, with **tree-covered** roads being particularly common. However, due to Jersey’s unique geographical position, most coverage features **sunny **weather.
All images were taken by a **Generation 2** camera.
clues.summary: Winding tree-covered lanes with hedgerows like English country roads, mostly sunny. All photos come from the older Gen 2 camera (grainy, dull colours).

clues.title: Plate: white front, yellow rear, no blue strip
text: Jersey licence plates follow the British model, having a long **white front** and **yellow rear** plate. In addition, you will notice the island’s red coat of arms on the left, as well as the letter ‘J’ at the beginning of all codes in unblurred plates.
NOTE: In contrast to the British mainland, Jersey was never a member of the European Union. This means that local plates do not have a blue strip.

images.caption: Black car with a yellow rear plate, right

clues.summary: British-style long plates, white at the front and yellow at the back, with a red coat of arms on the left and a J at the start of the code. No blue strip, unlike the UK mainland.

differs.how: UK plates have a blue strip; these have a red coat of arms

clues.title: Sign: UK-style signs and driving on the left
text: In general, road infrastructure is **similar **to that found in the United Kingdom. This includes driving on the [left](https://goo.gl/maps/fcPxAUuyzEzRf9Ak7), as well as [directional signs](https://goo.gl/maps/kNsowiMi9Dd68QKt5), [chevrons](https://goo.gl/maps/NBkNUYfGXL1baFQr8) and [warning signs](https://goo.gl/maps/dK5pbVjsHtbSjTAo6). Some of the subtle differences are discussed below.
clues.summary: Road signs, chevrons and warning signs look like the UK ones, and traffic drives on the left. Small differences are covered in the other clues.

differs.how: Subtle differences like yellow give-way lines and yellow phone booths

clues.title: Language: French-sounding street names
text: Due to its proximity to France, the vast majority of street and locality names contain **French **words. The island’s traditional language, known as [Jèrriais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A8rriais), is closely related to French and appears on some [signs](https://goo.gl/maps/gfXPVEU3CehwnLD79).
clues.summary: Most street and place names contain French words. The local language Jèrriais, close to French, appears on a few signs.

differs.how: Cars drive on the left and plates are British-style

clues.title: Houses: pastel walls, dark slate roofs
text: Similarly, the local **architecture **shares many characteristics with that of northern France. This includes pastel-coloured walls and dark slate roofs. However, [British-style](https://goo.gl/maps/j6uEGrojSRmpRXPS8) terraced houses are also common.
clues.summary: Buildings look like northern France, with pastel walls and dark slate roofs. British-style terraced houses are common too.

clues.title: Houses: red granite walls
text: Jersey is home to large reserves of **red granite**. As a result, it is a popular building material used for the construction of many **walls **and houses throughout the island.

images.caption: Red circle on the red-brown granite wall, top left, highlights the stone texture

clues.summary: Red granite is a popular building stone, used in many walls and houses across the island.

clues.title: Phone booth: yellow
text: In contrast to the iconic red booths found on the mainland of the UK,** telephone booths** in Jersey are uniquely yellow.
clues.summary: Phone booths are yellow, not the red ones of the UK mainland.

clues.title: Plants: Cornish palms, thin trunks, arching leaves
text: **Cornish palms** (Cordyline australis) can be identified by their distinctive thin trunks and arching leaves. They are commonly used as decorative plants on Jersey.
NOTE: These palms can also be found on some stretches of the British mainland’s coastline.
clues.summary: Palm-like plants with thin trunks and arching leaves, often planted for decoration. They also grow on some stretches of the British coast.

differs.how: Also found on some British coastlines

clues.title: Road lines: yellow give-way lines at junctions
text: Jersey uses **yellow give-way lines** at intersections.
NOTE: In contrast, the UK typically uses double dotted [white lines](https://goo.gl/maps/bKPN9mD7NQVUyoUi9) for this purpose.

images.caption: Red arrow points to the yellow give-way line painted across the road at the junction

clues.summary: Give-way lines at intersections are yellow. The UK normally uses double dotted white lines.

differs.how: UK give-way lines are double dotted white

clues.title: Sign: Green Lane and blue island-map markers
text: Jersey has an extensive network of cycling routes. Most notably, you will find [signs](https://goo.gl/maps/i9MW5htcqMZYhqRq9) referencing the start or end of a **“Green Lane”**. Blue [**route markers**](https://goo.gl/maps/kqz88wFjRsujGHFx5), containing a map of the island in the centre, are also common.
clues.summary: Cycling signs mention the start or end of a Green Lane. Blue route markers show a small island map in the centre.

clues.title: Sign: some signs hang off-centre on the post
text: Some road signs are **asymmetrically **attached to their signposts. This appears to be more prevalent on Jersey than on the British mainland.
NOTE: Keep in mind that this only applies to a minority of signs. Most are attached regularly.

images.caption: Children crossing warning sign hanging off-centre on its post; red circle zooms in on a sign at top left

clues.summary: A minority of road signs are attached to the post off-centre. This seems more common here than on the British mainland.

differs.how: Off-centre signs are less common in the UK

clues.title: Sign: street names with a coat of arms
text: Most street name signs in Jersey are adorned with the **coat of arms** of the parish in which they are located.
_You can click on the graphic to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Most street name signs carry a small coat of arms of the local parish.

clues.title: Landscape: urban area with taller buildings
text: Contrasting with the island’s typically rural look, the area surrounding the capital city of** St Helier** is more urbanised, featuring taller buildings, narrower streets and a more lively atmosphere.
clues.summary: Around the capital the look turns urban: taller buildings, narrower streets and more activity than the rural rest of the island.

clues.title: Landscape: large treeless area on the west coast
text: The Les Mielles Nature Reserve is a vast, **treeless **expanse located on Jersey’s western coast. Combined with the gentle westward slope and partially overcast coverage, this makes for a very recognisable area.
clues.summary: A vast treeless nature reserve on the west coast, with a gentle slope down to the west and often overcast skies.

clues.title: Coverage: greenish-purple glitch patches
text: Imagery containing a greenish-purple **discolouration **can be found in the southwest of the island.

NOTE: This glitch typically makes parts of the screen appear darker than they actually are. In addition, it blends into the landscape more seamlessly than [other glitches](https://goo.gl/maps/4B8quhU7FXLricWn7).
Moreover, this glitch is not unique to Jersey. It can be found in other countries as well.
clues.summary: Photos with a greenish-purple tint in the south-west. The glitch darkens parts of the screen and blends into the scenery. It also happens in other countries.

clues.title: Road: boundary fence along the airport
text: The roads surrounding **Jersey Airport** can be recognized thanks to the visible boundary **fence**.
clues.summary: Roads next to the airport have a visible boundary fence.

clues.title: Landmark: power station chimney on the south coast
text: The La Collette Power Station is located on a peninsula south of the capital. Its **chimney **can be seen from various points along the south coast and serves as a useful reference point for pinpointing.
clues.summary: The chimney of a power station on a peninsula south of the capital can be seen from many points along the south coast. Use it to pinpoint.

clues.title: Road: only divided road, maroon median
text: **Victoria Ave** runs along the island’s southern coast, immediately west of St Helier. It is the only **divided **road on Jersey and features a distinct maroon median.
clues.summary: The only divided road on the island, with a distinct maroon median. It runs along the south coast just west of the capital.

clues.title: Chevron: big yellow outline
text: In general, road infrastructure is similar to that found in the United Kingdom.
This includes driving on the left, as well as directional signs, chevrons and warning signs.
Chevrons often have a big yellow outline.

clues.summary: Chevron signs often have a big yellow outline. Other road signs look like the UK ones and traffic drives on the left.

differs.how: UK chevrons do not usually have a big yellow outline
